No towers. No SIM. Just air. When the internet goes dark, Q-P1NG Pro carries text over 433 MHz LoRa via a LilyGO T-Deck running our Swarm Protocol firmware. No 868/915 MHz build yet.
Broadcast storms kill naive meshes. Relays time each forward by signal, battery and channel load, and skip copies already sent.
The phone runs ZLIB + AES-256-GCM; the T-Deck relays ciphertext. Seized, it gives up its pairings and any active room, not your keys.
Fast BLE meets slow LoRa. Two-stage fragmentation, bounded queues and session cleanup keep the T-Deck's memory in check under packet loss.
The app puts only sealed text on LoRa. Images and files are refused, so the narrow band carries what matters.

Does Q-Cast work without the internet?
No. Q-Cast streams over the internet, Tor included. Off the grid, use RadioBridge or LoRa with their radio hardware.
Does the globe reveal my GPS location?
No. Q-Cast doesn't read your GPS. You pick the point yourself, and the station details and that place are public.
Can I keep my station Tor-only?
Yes. Broadcast and publish through Tor. A listing doesn't authorize a relay to put your audio on the open web.
Can my station grow beyond a few listeners?
Yes, through repeaters or an Icecast server. Direct mode serves three listeners. Q-P1NG offers no free unlimited hosting.
